answer: Identity verification can require completing a Wesolowski VDF: a long chain of modular squarings, each dependent on the previous result. GPUs may run separate chains for raven-like clones in parallel, but cannot shortcut one identity’s sequential delay; multiplying identities therefore consumes proportionally more compute and elapsed time. This physical bottleneck raises Sybil attack costs, while a verifier checks the proof efficiently. The karst of trust rests on a vertex of sequential work, not on an assumption that all parallel hardware is powerless.
